name: Trace minerals mixture; swine feed mineral mix; at processing plant
description: This unit process is a cradle-to-gate dataset of the production of a 1 kg of trace minerals mixture for swine feed in the US.

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Represents production at the national level.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: This unit process is a cradle-to-gate dataset of the production of a 1 kg of trace minerals mixture including 0.02 kg of Copper carbonate, at plant/RER WITH US ELECTRICITY U, 0.02 kg of Zinc monosulphate, ZnSO4.H2O, at plant/RER WITH US ELECTRICITY U, 0.92 kg of Limestone, milled, packed, at plant/CH WITH US ELECTRICITY U, 0.02 kg of Manganese oxide (Mn2O3), at plant/CN WITH US ELECTRICITY U, and 0.02 kg of Iron sulphate, at plant/RER WITH US ELECTRICITY U (from the US-EI 2.2 database).
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Life cycle inventory was originally assembled using the SimaPro software platform (Version 8.0.4.26) and was modified for submission using the OpenLCA platform (Version 1.3.0).
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: The unit process includes only materials (minerals) in a mineral mix.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Generic trace mineral mix for swine with limestone carrier.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Assumed equal quantites of minerals mixed with a limestone carrier.
processDocumentation.dataCollectionDescription: Data was collected during an ongoing project from 2013 through 2015.

sources.name: Development of Life Cycle Inventory data for U.S. Swine Production Scenarios

reviews.details: University of Arkansas swine dataset mapped to USLCI technosphere flows and FEDEFL elementary flows for publication on the Federal LCA Commons. Review covers mapping crosswalks, cutoff flows, and export structure.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: These data may be used in Situation C2, “Accounting without interactions.”  This is applicable to accounting studies that according to their goal definition do not include any interaction with other systems.
